So far i have sank 8 hours into this game and i have really enjoyed it, its truly good game and has the potential to be evolved into an outstanding moba, so here is my review of it. - To be honest, this is the most chill moba out there i have played and trust me i have played each and every one of the already existing ones, i am huge moba fan and veteran. I have more than 12,000.0 hours in Dota2, immortal player, i have been challenger in LoL, top 5 grandmaster in Heroes of the storm, mythic glory in mobile legends, 1900 rating in HoN, bloodline champions, smite , strife, realm of the titans and so on, basicly i have played almost every moba that existed. As i am already older, i prefer to play more chill games than sweaty ones, Sirocco manages to be intriguing, taking the already good elements of moba games while removing the sweaty attacking, because here your ship automatically fires. I cant lie, i am sucker for moba type of games and this is surely one of the reason i got pulled in but Sirocco is really something different than your usual moba, it plays different yet at the same time the core elements remain the same, you have creeps, towers and throne(core), you have lanes etc.If you are looking for a more relaxing moba then this is very good choice, its much more relaxing than Heroes of the storm which is considered the most easy. If i had to rate the tutorial though id give it no more than 2/5, maybe its okay for completely new players but for a veteran like me it was bad, it gives no important specifics for a moba veteran, it will just tell you the MOST basics things. I wish the tutorial had explained that weapons have linear progression while the ships dont, the ships have rotation each game and while you can play with each ship every game certain ship requires different amount of ship upgrades in order to be acquired, i wish it had told me that the ship itself doesnt fire, but as a new player i asked myself alot of times if my ship has default fire attack or its the weapons, because it would fire alot of things so i couldnt see how it is, then i went into practice and i understood how weapons work, this is not told in the tutorial, basicly weapons fire automatically but every weapon has special, this special happens when the very same weapon hits several times, this also has not been included in the tutorial, to me its still not clear if towers give occo or not, even though i played alot of games, there are many things that left unexplained and left for you to figure out, i understand the tutorial is to give you most basic things, but as i said for me as a moba veteran it basicly gave me no more than one important information and that was about the harvesters, other than that i felt that i completely wasted my time watching it. The game is truly great, the ui is good enough. SHIPS > the ships are like heroes, they are different enough from each other, the weapons however are rather boring, i believe they will add more but for now they are not very interesting, nothing huge game breaking. The only thing that may be frustrating for new players is that alot of the ships have hooks, latches and alot of displacement tools, for me it was fine, i think there should be ships like that but i definitely felt like it can be quite punishing if you dont know the ships that have escapes in order to counter hooks, barriers etc. They are fine the way they are so far for me, but id suggest that the new ships are more oriented to anything else but displacement tools, the ships that already have displacement tools should stay the way they are so they are UNIQUE, adding more displacement tools will remove the uniqueness of such ships, there are alot of ideas, i am sure the developers have good grasp of what can and must be included when it comes to new ships and weapons. WEAPONS > Not diverse enough, not many choices, basicly if i want to play ranged type of dps i have no more than 3 good weapons to put in my arsenal, its boring, i expected more diversity on this side but since its early access i guess it will be included more in the future Ship and weapon progression system Its fine, the game overall chooses to be chill and slow, most of the times you wont be one shooted by weapons, yes there are abilities that do 50% of your hp but weapons are predictable and rarely you will see someone take more than 20% of your health in instant, i like this take on the system but still weapons are boring and you dont have meaningful choices, captains are also boring and not diverse enough To conclude, i am really really enjoying this game, i am writing this review in mind that this game is still in early access, it will get much better, i can see that the developers are very passionate for this game and they truly understand alot of the things that must be done in order for their game to be good. Give this game a shot, it deserves it, there are alot of interesting things to mess up with and i am sure as time goes that weapons will also be more interesting! I cant wait to see how this game evolves, more ships, more skins, more captains, more weapons.

Sirocco is my favorite new game of the last several years. It's easy enough to get into game and have fun, especially for those with former MOBA experience, but it's also not too much to learn even for someone without. New players have a good shot of having fun in their first game, and that's more than I can say about most Mobas. Yet despite the casual-friendly nature of the game, Sirocco also has an impressive strategic and mechanical depth that results in some very satisfying high-level games. I highly recommend checking out the vods for our recent community tournament (available in the discord server) to see some of the strategic gameplay possible in a more coordinated setting than solo Q. As a longtime (5000 hour+) league of legends player, Sirocco offers similar peaks, without so much of the micro-intensive earlygame & less severe snowballing. Having an earlygame lead definitely helps, you'll be higher level and with more upgrades than your opponents, but long death timers and scaling damage mean that the game is never over till it's over. Losing in League can often feel like the game has been over for 20 minutes and you're just forced to suffer until the official conclusion, Sirocco doesn't share that issue. Death timers are long enough in lategame that one solid pick can give your team the opportunity to start the comeback! The game certainly isn't perfect, but for an early access product out for only a month I've been extremely impressed by the quality of games I've played & the friends I've made in the community, and the patches that the dev team have put out have been nearly perfect in addressing what the community wants to see, both balance-wise and in new features. I'd highly recommend anybody to login and play a few games and see what they think, then leave a positive review of your own once you're hooked!

Mixed bag, mostly saltwater. Review at 98 hours at time posting (Main + alt) Would I recommend? No... but maybe in the future. Balance is all over the place. Some boats (Horizon, Nautilus) are niche and require building to shore up weaknesses in their kits, while others (Lockjaw, Stingray, Lurker) are overloaded. Snowballing is brutal. Most games are effectively decided in the first 5 minutes you just don’t lose until 30 minutes later. There's no real comeback mechanic once structures fall. You can delay, but you won’t win. Split-pushing dominates the meta. Teamfights are flashy distractions the real wins happen quietly on the side lanes. Leaver penalties are a half-measure. Patch 0.9.1 tried to address it, but didn’t solve why people are leaving in the first place. I’ve left my fair share usually because the match was already lost and I didn’t want to sit through a 40-minute slow bleed. No in-game communication. At all. Combined with a 3-player party cap, you’re always relying on two randoms who may or may not decide to go 1/15/4 in the default boat. Weapon upgrades feel weak. They scale poorly compared to ability upgrades (which level automatically), meaning some boats can dominate just by staying in lane with nearly zero investment. Despite all this, I’ve sunk nearly 100 hours into the game across two accounts. That should say something. Sirocco has a strong core, but the match quality and lack of real strategic depth in most games keeps it from being great. If the devs addressed balance, comeback potential, and team coordination (like basic chat!), it could sail much further.

The UI doesn't adequately prioritize important information like active (de)buffs, and weapon cool-downs. The balancing is comical right now. No amount of careful upgrade planning can circumvent lane-wide homing lasers when the best your ship can do is teleport 2 feet once in a blue moon. Snowballing happens within the first few minutes of the game, and since there are no mobs outside of lane, the best you can do is scrape for XP while staring down the dominating player. Occo is the most valuable resource for gaining strength, but you have practically no hope of acquiring it once the opposite team starts to gain leverage, all the while they're drowning in it. The visibility system feels far too aggressive, especially for the lack of individual control you have over those stats. Non-XP weapon upgrades feel like pushing a boulder up a hill, and shop weapons in general feel horribly unimportant in player fights. The menus are a mess of text. Sure you can just memorize every piece of information, or you can do the human thing and pull out your reading glasses and a cup of tea for the novel you've been served.

[h1] 🌊 Sirocco – A Hidden Gem in Early Access [/h1] Sirocco is one of those games that sparks different reactions — and for good reason (mostly though it's the growing part and the social interaction with ladder that sparks these reactions). You’ll find mixed reviews here and there, but considering it's still in early access, I genuinely believe it’s one of the few titles that captures the true spirit of what early access should be. You can feel the potential, and more importantly, the path to that potential is actively being paved. 🚤 [b] A Diverse Arsenal of Boats [/b] Sirocco boasts an impressive variety of boats, each with a clear identity and purpose — from assassin-style boats to tanky frontliners, supportive builds, long-range snipers, and close-combat bruisers. No matter your playstyle, there’s a boat that fits you. And on top of that, the boat designs? Just awesome. Each one has a distinct flair that adds to the game's personality. 🔊[b] Exceptional Sound Design [/b] This is where Sirocco really shines. It’s not just about the music fitting the naval theme — it's the way sound is integrated into gameplay. Effects from boats like Horizon, Dragonfly, and Aurora aren’t just background noise; they actively enhance immersion and inform your gameplay. The sound design helps build tension, deliver impact, and make each moment feel alive on the water. 🔄[b] Comeback Mechanics Done Right [/b] One of the most exciting elements is how games can swing. Falling behind doesn’t mean it's over — a single mistake from the leading team can turn the tide completely. This makes every match feel dynamic and rewarding, especially when you’re coordinating with friends in voice chat. Strategic talk, laughter, hype moments — shout out to Civi, Ward, and Shadow Masquerade for all the fun gameplay, #NorwegianVikings. 💬 [b] Transparent, Passionate Devs [/b] The developers are among the most transparent and community-focused I’ve seen. They're active on Discord, quick to respond to feedback, and unafraid to stick to a long-term vision — even if not everyone agrees right away. That kind of integrity and interaction is rare, and it adds a lot of trust and momentum to the development process. ⚙️[b] What Could Improve [/b] Low Player Base: Queue times, especially at higher MMR, can get long. This is understandable in early access, but hopefully as more players discover the game, matchmaking will become faster and more consistent. Matchmaking Balance: With a small community, striking the right balance between fair match-ups and reasonable wait times is tough. This is a delicate issue in most early-access PvP games, but continued tweaking will be key to long-term health. Teammate vs. Enemy Spells & Audio Cues: Many boats already have clear audio or visual cues built in, but there are still some where it's hard to tell the difference between teammate and enemy abilities — Wither's Q, for example, can be a bit confusing in the heat of battle. Making these distinctions even clearer would greatly improve moment-to-moment game-play. The sound design for Aurora, Horizon, and Dragonfly is fantastic, but adding a unique audio or visual indicator to differentiate between friendly and enemy spell effects would be a great quality-of-life improvement. Also, the devs would earn major bonus points for integrating additional universal design features in the future — for example, an option for players who are hard of hearing to enable visual indicators for key audio-based mechanics. It may not be the highest priority right now, but it would be a meaningful addition down the line as the game grows. 🧭 [b] Final Thoughts [/b] Sirocco is one of the rare cases where early access feels right. The foundation is solid, updates are consistent, and the systems in place — from boat mechanics to augments, coils, weapons, and map objectives — show clear depth and intentional design. Yes, it still needs polish. Yes, on-boarding for new players could be smoother (though honestly, if you watch the 90-second tutorial video and give it 3–5 hours, it really starts to click). But the vision is there. And more importantly: it’s fun. I’m especially looking forward to the day when full-party play is supported — coordinated teams are where this game will really thrive, and it's fun (I recommend joining the Sirocco Discord, you'll find people to play with for sure if that is something you'd want, and there is plenty of players that will teach you tips and tricks). This is a game built to last. If you’re looking for a unique, tactical, team-based game with developer heart behind it, anchor your boat here. Sirocco may still be finding its sea legs, but I believe it's sailing in the right direction, and hey, if your sail is broken, craft a new one in the crafting menu. ;)

For now I will say 'no' to Sirocco. Why? First some context on where I come from with MOBAs; played League for a long time (over level 500), played Vainglory, Heroes of the Storm, Predecessor, a bit of Dota 2, Eternal Return, Smite and Smite 2, Battlerite. Why does that matter? Cause 1 it shows I am the target audience for this kinda game, but 2 I can point to a major flaw here that I think will be the undoing of the game if it were to get a bigger playerbase; a lack of 'heroes' to identify with. This isn't the 'I need to see myself represented' talk, this is more literal- you need SOMETHING to form an attachment with. Captains aren't much beyond mechanics, stats, etc and a picture. This means the ships are the big appeal but they aren't really. Ships feel more like guns in valorant or another shooter. The change the feel, and maybe some mechanics, but ultimate you don't play those games generally just for 'gun'. This is why 'mains' exist in MOBAs, people gravitate to a character be it their kit, lore, voicelines, or visual design. By making it something you can change as you upgrade, one it generalizes the whole thing, but it also means you might have to build up to the actual ship you'd want to play, I think another big issue is the autofiring mechanic just isn't better than say general basic attack on mouse click in other mobas or a dedicated button press. It makes the things unreliable (not to mention swapping weapons in the shop will switch the oldest, so if I want to swap the second weapon I have to select the new one, then select my first weapon again that I wanted to keep. Its just a bit of jank that slows it down and makes it clunky). Add to this a lack of recall and really jankily shaped middle area that could probably use an open area with in the middle for more brawling- and while I didn't dislike Sirocco, it was not a very memorable experience compared to any of the other mobas mentioned above. I do hope if nothing else that it will find a niche, but I don't see a game like this even competing the the naval fans circles either. Some cool ships here and there isn't really enough to combat a generic overall feel with a bit of jank. Key points -Lack of 'personality'/'champions' to get attached to and vibe with as a player as all ships become available throughout a match (which also means if you DO like a particular ship you might not be able to play it till late) -Clunky/absent mechanics, like no recall, unreliable basic attacks, abilities not hitting their target or not feeling like they function in a very legible way (Prism for example has a deflect that doesn't show very clearly how it is working, and my personal favorite Lockjaw for some reason can hook it's own allies instead of just enemies making it's hooks fun but janky) -Map could use a few changes, the middle areas is VERY cramped and doesn't feel good to navigate. That said the announcer was pretty good, and for a general game it's not bad, this by no means is 'Sirocco is bad', Sirocco is simply just 'okay', and I don't think that's super worth while with so many other options for most people.

Very much not for me. The amount of "wtf happened?" just makes the time spend seem wasted. Three abilities per boat, 6 upgrades per ability and with 20 boats that can be changed almost any time of the game, either makes you want to learn or give up. My biggest annoyance is the lack of predictability and counterplay. Suddenly a boat pulls you into enemy 3 boats, a tornado keeps you there and you die. Other times a wall of ice and a blizzard from out of nowhere kills you. A harpoon from fog of war takes 50% of your health. Then you can heal and another harpoon does exactly the same. Why is the enemy stronger than you? You don't know. Is it the boat, the upgrades, the weapons, the gold, the captain or just a skill issue? No idea! Keep distance - still die. Low health enemy that you think you can kill? - Wrong, you're dead. The theme of the game; being a boat that attacks other boats and have abilities and push lanes is fun. The skill ramp just invites me to either dedicate too much time, before I can have fun, or uninstall and play another game where I actually have fun. In this case I went with option number two.
